notes: Sample users.json - the credential registry. Copy to users.json and edit. It holds WHO the tool logs in as, never WITH WHAT: every password is a 'password_ref' naming a key in data/encrypted_secret_text.json, resolved at run time.

Three sections, because three different things are logged into: 'database_credentials' (a database engine), 'remote_credentials' (a machine, over SSH or WinRM), and 'monitor_users' (an account on a neighbouring tool the DBA also owns, recorded so it is not lost - nothing connects with these).

'credential_name' is how every other file refers to one credential. db_instances.json points at it by 'default_credential_name', sql_targets.json by 'credential_name', cmd_access blocks by 'credential_name'. Keep it unique and keep it stable - renaming one silently breaks every file that names it.

'server_id' ties a credential block to an entry in db_instances.json. One machine may carry several credentials with different roles; the instance's 'default_credential_name' picks which one is used when a caller does not say.
An SSH key credential leaves 'password_ref' empty and is resolved through the key file instead - keep key files out of the repository (data/ssh_keys/ is ignored).

The tool needs far less than an administrator on a monitored instance. The least-privilege grants per engine are in docs/security.md; the short form is a read-only login plus the server-level view permissions the metric SQL reads.

credentials.notes: Read-only login used by metric collection. Preferred over the DBA login for anything scheduled: a monitoring pass should not be able to change the instance it is measuring.
GRANT pg_monitor is enough for every PostgreSQL metric in the catalog.

remote_credentials.server_description: Windows host - OS metrics and maintenance over WinRM

credentials.notes: A domain service account, not a personal one: a scheduled job authenticating as a person breaks the day that person leaves.

remote_credentials.server_description: Linux host - OS metrics and backup scripts over SSH
Linux host - SSH key authentication, no password

credentials.notes: Key authentication via data/ssh_keys/oracle-lab.key. An empty password_ref is what says 'use the key', so do not fill it in with a placeholder.

monitor_users.note: Recorded so the account is not lost with the person who created it. Nothing in the toolkit logs in here.
monitor_users.name: monitor-acme_grafana_admin
